```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
billboard |> 
  select(artist, track, date.entered, wk1:wk4)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
n_val <- sum(!is.na(billboard$wk6))
ggplot(billboard, aes(x = wk6)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Week 6 Rankings",
    subtitle = paste0("n = ", n_val, " songs"),
    x = "Week 6 Rank",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

```{r}
billboard |> 
  select(wk1, wk4, wk10, wk20, wk40, wk76) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "week", values_to = "rank") |> 
  mutate(week = fct_inorder(week)) |> 
  group_by(week) |> 
  summarize(
    present = sum(!is.na(rank)),
    missing = sum(is.na(rank))
  )
```

```{r}
billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"), 
    names_to = "week", 
    values_to = "rank"
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(rank)) |> 
  mutate(week = as.integer(str_remove(week, "wk"))) |> 
  arrange(artist, track, week) |> 
  group_by(artist, track) |> 
  summarize(
    re_entered = any(diff(week) > 1), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  count(re_entered)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
billboard_long <- billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "rank",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |> 
  mutate(week = as.integer(str_remove(week, "wk")))

ggplot(billboard_long, aes(x = week, y = rank, group = interaction(artist, track))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.25) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "Song Rankings Over Time",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Rank (reversed)"
  )
```

```{r}
#| message: false
# Create song-level summary
song_summary <- billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "rank",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |> 
  mutate(week = as.integer(str_remove(week, "wk"))) |> 
  group_by(artist, track) |> 
  summarize(
    first_rank = rank[which.min(week)],
    best_rank = min(rank),
    first_week_at_best = min(week[rank == best_rank]),
    total_weeks = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Print a preview of the song-level summary
print("Preview of Song-Level Summary:")
head(song_summary)

# Identify the three notable songs
fastest_no1 <- song_summary |> 
  filter(best_rank == 1) |> 
  slice_min(first_week_at_best, n = 1)

slowest_no1 <- song_summary |> 
  filter(best_rank == 1) |> 
  slice_max(first_week_at_best, n = 1)

longest_run_top10 <- song_summary |> 
  filter(best_rank <= 10) |> 
  slice_max(total_weeks, n = 1)

# Combine and display
print("Notable Songs:")
bind_rows(
  fastest_no1 |> mutate(notable_category = "Fastest to #1"),
  slowest_no1 |> mutate(notable_category = "Slowest to #1"),
  longest_run_top10 |> mutate(notable_category = "Longest Run in Top 10")
) |> 
  select(notable_category, artist, track, first_rank, best_rank, first_week_at_best, total_weeks)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
#| message: false
# Filter for songs that reached the top 10
top10_songs <- billboard_long |> 
  group_by(artist, track) |> 
  filter(min(rank) <= 10) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    highlight = case_when(
      artist == "Madonna" & track == "Music" ~ "Madonna - Music (Fastest to #1)",
      artist == "Lonestar" & track == "Amazed" ~ "Lonestar - Amazed (Slowest to #1)",
      artist == "Creed" & track == "Higher" ~ "Creed - Higher (Longest Top-10 Run)",
      TRUE ~ "Other Top-10 Songs"
    )
  )

# Plot top 10 songs, highlighting the three notable ones
ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(top10_songs, highlight == "Other Top-10 Songs"),
    aes(x = week, y = rank, group = interaction(artist, track)),
    color = "lightgray", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(top10_songs, highlight != "Other Top-10 Songs"),
    aes(x = week, y = rank, group = interaction(artist, track), color = highlight),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Madonna - Music (Fastest to #1)" = "#E41A1C",
      "Lonestar - Amazed (Slowest to #1)" = "#377EB8",
      "Creed - Higher (Longest Top-10 Run)" = "#4DAF4A"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Song Trajectories for Top-10 Billboard Hits",
    subtitle = "Highlighting three notable songs",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Rank (reversed)",
    color = "Notable Songs"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
